post_title: How many active New World screwworm cases will Mexico's Senasica dashboard report in late October 2026?

question.title: How many active New World screwworm cases will Mexico's Senasica dashboard report in late October 2026?
question.description:
New World screwworm (NWS; Spanish: gusano barrenador del ganado, GBG) is a parasitic fly (Cochliomyia hominivorax) whose larvae burrow into the living tissue of warm-blooded animals, causing potentially fatal myiasis. The pest re-emerged in Mexico in November 2024 after decades of regional eradication, and has since spread widely. Mexico's National Service for Agro-Alimentary Health, Safety, and Quality (Senasica) publishes a public Power BI dashboard tracking active cases by state (entidad) and municipality.

Senasica defines a case as "active" at the time of diagnosis; after 15 days it is revisited and reclassified as inactive if personnel verify there are no new wounds or larvae. The national active-case count has fluctuated over 2026: roughly 692 active cases at the start of January 2026, a reduction reported through early 2026, then a renewed rise through the summer and autumn. Reported snapshots include about 1,885 active (early June 2026), about 1,951 (mid-July 2026), roughly 2,055 total in early October 2026, and 1,968 as of the report updated October 16, 2026 (epidemiological week 41). By mid-October 2026, 30 of Mexico's 32 states had recorded cases, with Chihuahua, Oaxaca, Puebla, Chiapas and Sonora among the highest. Cumulative cases since the 2024 re-emergence exceeded 47,000 in Mexico. The US CDC reported over 209,400 cumulative animal cases and over 2,600 human cases across Mexico and Central America as of early October 2026.

Mexico has deployed sterile-fly releases, intensified surveillance, and movement controls to suppress the outbreak. Because active-case counts reflect both new detections and the 15-day reclassification cycle, the weekly total can move up or down depending on the balance of new outbreaks versus resolved cases. The dashboard's "Casos activos" headline total is updated roughly weekly and shows an "Informe actualizado al:" date.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of active New World screwworm (Gusano Barrenador del Ganado, GBG) cases in Mexico ("Casos activos") shown on Senasica's official Power BI dashboard ("Casos activos por entidad y municipio") at https://app.powerbi.com/view?r=eyJrIjoiMjkzMzAzMzUtZmRlNi00ZTMzLTk1NDEtNjkzZTEwNzZjZGFlIiwidCI6ImM1OWRjNTZhLTkzZWMtNGIwNy1iNzFkLTQzYzg0NDkyNTcxOCIsImMiOjR9 — specifically, the single national "Casos activos" headline total displayed on the dashboard whose "Informe actualizado al:" date is the latest date on or before October 31, 2026. For example, a dashboard showing "1,968 Casos activos" resolves as 1968.
question.fine_print: The "Casos activos" figure is Senasica's own count: a case is counted as active at the time of diagnosis and is revisited after 15 days, becoming inactive if personnel verify the absence of new wounds or larvae. Whatever national total the dashboard displays for the most recent report dated on or before October 31, 2026 (typically updated weekly by epidemiological week) is used, regardless of how it is distributed across species, states, or municipalities. If the dashboard is temporarily unavailable, the same headline figure as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) citing Senasica for the report dated on or before October 31, 2026 will be used. If Senasica permanently ceases publishing an active-case total and no credible source reports the figure, the question is annulled.
